::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 25. 1867.  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS.55387 (1): P. 389
:::

Dear Miss Yonge	
The parcel for [Miss Lewis](people/person_873.qmd) reached Tooting safely, and will not in the least inconvenience [me](people/person_939.qmd).[^1] I will endeavour to deliver it early after my arrival.

I have read the [Story of the Scotch girl](organizations/other_193.qmd). It is very interesting - rather sensational in fact. [Robespierre](people/person_2420.qmd), [Danton](people/person_2421.qmd), [Napoleon](people/person_2207.qmd), the Guillotine 'La Lanterne,' a sprinkling of smugglers with a slight dash of wreckers, highly toned Irish, Scotch, French nationalities, a mad woman, suicide, a murder or two &c &c. make up a dish that certainly cannot be considered savourless. There is no great reach of <u>thought</u>, as [Mrs Lewes](people/person_1994.qmd), or [Mrs Gaskell](people/person_1965.qmd) have, nor anything like grace & delicacy of touch of [Miss Thackeray](people/person_1240.qmd) but it looks to me vigorous firm drawing. I am getting a friend, a critic by profession to look at it. My reading was too much in novel reading vein to enable me to judge. Besides it was done between 11p.m. and 2 a.m. after a [*illegible*] of day 

We shall communicate direct with her. 

Yours very sincerely
A. Macmillan

---

[^1]: CMY had asked him to deliver an illumination to her friend Miss Lewis in Philadelphia.
